luckGekisou.primaryGoal: Complete canonical Top-K proof for the original LUCK Gekisou requests within 20 seconds end to end.
luckGekisou.classificationMethod: Read each original request execution.gekisou and scenario.musicId; verify execution.scoreId belongs to that MasterLiveMusic row and exists in MasterLiveMusicScore and the pinned chart payload. Match the three _gekisouMission fields to the three actual chart fever intervals. Include only enabled requests with at least one mission value 2 (LUCK). Case names are not used to classify.
luckGekisou.finding: Both runtimes complete 0 of 18 LUCK Score requests and 3 of 18 LUCK nonlinear requests. All three completed cases use clientEventPoints and were already complete at the baseline. No newly completed LUCK case is established by this public CI comparison.

scope.inputProvenance: PR40 real published game charts/tables with three fixed hypothetical inventories, not player-account exports
scope.method: Rehashed archives, every FILES inventory entry, pinned PR40 git definitions, snapshot/roster/request pure reconstruction against existing native preparation; read every per-case report and answer; exact-rational certificate intersections and complete canonical ordered team comparisons. No solver, build, native preparation or performance run.

timingScope.browser: processWallMs: Node page.evaluate invocation through the final Worker response; includes input transport, Worker creation, WASM initialization, dataset/DeckSolver construction and recommendation. Excludes host fixture reads, HTTP server/browser startup and browser installation.
timingScope.native: processWallMs: native process spawn through process exit; includes process startup, input reads, dataset construction, recommendation and output persistence. Excludes benchmark runner startup and host-side result validation.

scope.oracle: notRun; agreement and non-disjoint certificates are compatibility evidence, not an independent global ranking or game-parity oracle
scope.causality: One CI repetition per source/runtime. CPU models and software are reported separately; elapsed ratios alone do not isolate algorithmic changes. Timeout durations are right-censored.
